meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided my son's essay was worth a zero, and when?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero? What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you actually have.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, the night of October 28. Students write in another file and paste it in, Hale. That proves when it was pasted, not who wrote it.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.

Fine, the history stands for what it shows, and whatever happens, this stays off his record and stays quiet. As for the line, seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. A bad citation is a bad citation.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft. That's what an outline is for. And you still haven't answered me on that line from the play.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Like being stuck is not a wrong answer, Hale, it's a nervous seventeen-year-old's answer. So he was heard on November 2, and the zero went in the next day. What are you proposing?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay with a week behind it. Of course they don't match. I asked what you're proposing.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, a date this week, the new mark entered well before December 1. In writing tonight, Hale.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Okay. Thursday after school, marked within two days, and it all goes in tonight's email. Who supervises him?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
We do, once that email names who's in the room with him. Thursday, private, nothing on file.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay this Thursday after school, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record under procedure 4.4. I still require the name of the person supervising him, and confirmation that this will not happen in front of his class. I expect all of this in writing from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday with the new mark replacing the zero, and she still wants the supervisor named and the terms in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, then offering to look at any weekend draft Owen had, because that answered her only defence with something she could check.
What cost ground: opening with the checker score and saying the zero stands, because it gave her a machine's number to attack and a decision made before anyone was heard.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on the late night of October 28, close to that memory, which is why she went short and hard there; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she called the invented Act 3 line a simple misquote, answer it directly by showing there is no real line it could be a garbled version of, so that piece stands instead of staying open.
